title: OpenAI Acquires Astral (uv, ruff, ty)
description: OpenAI announced acquisition of Astral, the company behind uv, ruff, and ty—three increasingly critical open source projects in the Python ecosystem. Simon Willison shares thoughts on this significant development for Python tooling.
author: Simon Willison

title: Running Qwen 397B Locally Using Apple's 'LLM in a Flash' Techniques
description: Dan Woods successfully ran Qwen3.5-397B-A17B at 5.5+ tokens/second on a 48GB MacBook Pro M3 Max using techniques from Apple's 2023 'LLM in a flash' paper. The Mixture-of-Experts model streams expert weights from SSD, with 5.5GB staying resident in memory. Dan used Claude Code with the autoresearch pattern to run 90 experiments and produce MLX Objective-C and Metal code.
author: Simon Willison

title: Snowflake Cortex AI Prompt Injection Vulnerability
description: Simon Willison discusses a prompt injection attack in Snowflake's Cortex Agent that allowed execution of malicious code via process substitution despite allow-lists. The attack highlights inherent unreliability of pattern-based allow-lists and reinforces the need for deterministic sandboxes operating outside the agent layer.
author: Simon Willison

title: Agentic Engineering Patterns: Subagents
description: Simon Willison explores the subagents pattern for handling larger tasks without burning through too much of the coding agent's valuable top-level context. Subagents provide a simple but effective way to manage LLM context limits (generally around 1M tokens) while maintaining quality results below 200K tokens.
author: Simon Willison

title: OpenAI Codex Subagents Generally Available
description: OpenAI Codex announced general availability of subagents after several weeks of preview. The feature includes default subagents for 'explorer', 'worker', and 'default', plus support for custom agents defined as TOML files. The subagents pattern is now widely supported across coding agents including Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Mistral Vibe, OpenCode, VS Code, and Cursor.
author: Simon Willison

title: Coding Agents for Data Analysis Workshop
description: Simon Willison presented a NICAR 2026 workshop on using coding agents (Claude Code and OpenAI Codex) for data analysis. The three-hour session covered asking questions against databases, exploring data, cleaning data, creating visualizations, and scraping data with agents. Participants used GitHub Codespaces with budget-restricted Codex API keys.
author: Simon Willison

title: Mistral Small 4 Released: 119B Parameter Apache 2 Licensed Model
description: Mistral released Mistral Small 4, a new Apache 2 licensed 119B parameter Mixture-of-Experts model (6B active parameters). The model unifies capabilities of flagship models: Magistral for reasoning, Pixtral for multimodal, and Devstral for agentic coding. It supports reasoning_effort='none' or 'high' modes.
author: Simon Willison

title: 1M Context Now Generally Available for Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6
description: Anthropic announced 1M token context is now generally available for Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6 models. Notably, standard pricing applies across the full 1M window with no long-context premium, unlike competitors OpenAI and Gemini which charge more for prompts above certain token thresholds (200K for Gemini 3.1 Pro, 272K for GPT-5.4).
author: Simon Willison
